input: This work represents a remarkable advancement in pressure-sensor technology. These measurement boundaries delimit the reported sensor metrics. We have not performed a statistical hypothesis test. There was no resolvable change in film thickness. We observed a larger contact area under load by optical imaging after treatment. This means the treatment proves that contact area is the only origin of the improved sensitivity. However, the mechanical modulus was not measured and changes in bulk stiffness therefore cannot be ruled out. A matched-modulus control would help distinguish these explanations. Optical imaging showed a larger contact area under load after treatment, with no resolvable change in film thickness. These observations are consistent with a contribution from increased contact area, but they do not establish it as the sole cause of the sensitivity increase: mechanical modulus was not measured, leaving changes in bulk stiffness as a possible explanation. A matched-modulus control could help distinguish these explanations, but has not yet been performed. The sensor retained 94% of its initial response after 200 loading cycles at 1 kPa, demonstrating response retention under these conditions without establishing long-term durability.
